> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/currency-fraction-digits.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be91d11c842b2224db031c9fb404dc9425399a26` — the merge of head `0e006877963089d9c1f90b18a69614a15b3578b8` into base `1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be91d11c842b2224db031c9fb404dc9425399a26 && git checkout be91d11c842b2224db031c9fb404dc9425399a26
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a 0e006877963089d9c1f90b18a69614a15b3578b8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a && git merge --no-ff 0e006877963089d9c1f90b18a69614a15b3578b8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1c8b320a894b31dcfc76c33c8e7a62b8986d893a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e006877963089d9c1f90b18a69614a15b3578b8`

### ① Derived judgments

- **The deleted guard is exactly the #7918 FIELD-level anchor and nothing else.** `git diff origin/main 0e006877 -- packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` has two hunks: the import comment (`:31-34`) and the `FieldSchema.superRefine` block that read `field.type === 'currency' && field.precision !== undefined && field.currencyConfig?.currencyMode === 'fixed'` → `currencyPrecisionContradiction(defaultCurrency, precision)` → `ctx.addIssue({ path: ['precision'] })` (main `:2314-2333`), now a comment. The removed code only ever ADDED an issue (no transform), so every previously accepted field's output is byte-identical, as the changeset says. Right. Merge-base `172b4cf3`..head is exactly the 6 files in `diff.patch`; the 3 commits main gained since (`1c8b320a`) touch none of them (identical per-file line counts in `git diff --stat origin/main..head` for those six).
- **What now parses that was refused before — measured, head vs origin/main `field.zod.ts` in a detached probe worktree (`probe.mts`, same node_modules).** 30-row matrix (`probe-head.jsonl` / `probe-main.jsonl`; main = head's tree with `origin/main:field.zod.ts` swapped in, blob `8f35ae5d` → `26f8ef39` restored, `git diff HEAD` empty). Refused→accepted, with the authored value carried: fixed USD `precision` 18 / 1 / 0, fixed JPY 2 / 18, fixed KWD 2 / 15, fixed with defaulted CNY 0, and `ObjectSchema.create` + JSON re-parse with fixed-USD 18 (main threw at `fields.amount.precision`; head keeps 18). Unchanged verdict AND message on every other row: agreeing values (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3), fail-open BTC 8, dynamic / defaulted-mode / no-`currencyConfig`, absent `precision`, `precision: 2.5` (int guard), `scale: 2` on currency (still refused at `['scale']`, #19629), `number` 18, `number` 1+`scale` 2, `percent` 0+`scale` 3. Two rows still refuse with a SHORTER issue list: `precision: -1` (main: int guard + contradiction; head: int guard only) and both keys authored (below). All 13 accepted-on-both rows are byte-identical (`JSON.stringify` equal). So the widening is exactly "field-level integer `precision` ≠ the fixed currency's CLDR fraction digits, known codes only" and nothing else.
- **`currencyConfig.precision` anchor (#19992's region) refuses exactly as before.** Call sites at head `field.zod.ts:466` (`.superRefine`) and `:506` (`.overwrite`), identical text to main `:465`/`:505` (one-line shift from the import comment; no hunk in `CurrencyConfigSchema`, `SelectOptionSchema` or the `requiredWhen`/`readonlyWhen` region). Probed at head, same as main: `currencyConfig: { precision: 2, currencyMode: 'fixed', defaultCurrency: 'JPY' }` and `KWD` refused at `['currencyConfig','precision']` with "currency JPY has 0 fraction digits; `precision: 2` contradicts it …"; `{ precision: 0, currencyMode: 'fixed' }` (defaulted CNY) refused; the `scale` alias under `currencyConfig` still refused as an unrecognized key with the `precision` suggestion; agreeing USD 2 accepted with identical output. With BOTH keys authored (field `precision: 2` + `currencyConfig.precision: 2`, fixed JPY): main raised two issues, head raises exactly one, at `['currencyConfig','precision']` — the field is still refused. Right.
- **The premise is TRUE at the objectui pin `f8a9d0fb0596` (`.objectui-sha` on main and head).** `git grep -n -w precision f8a9d0fb -- 'packages/**/*.ts{,x}' 'apps/**/*.ts{,x}'` minus tests = 83 lines; the 27 non-comment lines are: type declarations (`types/src/field-types.ts:407,436,446`, `form-spec.ts:191`), i18n labels, `formatPercent`/`formatPercentBody`'s own parameter name (`fields/src/index.tsx:588-659`; its callers pass `scale`, a pattern-derived `decimals`, or `undefined`), pass-through copies into field meta (`ObjectGrid.tsx:2863,3084,3250`, `RelatedList.tsx:1607`, `RecordDetailPanel.tsx:167`, `sectionFields.ts:321`, `ObjectGallery.tsx:367`, `fieldEnrichment.ts:231`, `useColumnSummary.ts:492` — built into `columnHints` and never read by `formatSummaryLabel`), and the one WRITER `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:917-919` (`patchDef({ precision: v })`, comment `:287` calls it the field-level TOTAL digit count). Faces read: `CurrencyField.tsx:80` `fractionDigits = currency ? currencyFractionDigits(currency) : 2` (neither key); `NumberCellRenderer` `index.tsx:772` `numField.scale`; `PercentCellRenderer` `:852` `scale ?? 0`; `formatCurrency(value, currency?, locale?)` (`:472`) takes no width and is what the grid footer's currency arm calls (`useColumnSummary.ts` currency arm; percent arm `column?.scale ?? 0`); `ObjectMetricWidget.tsx` resolves only the currency (`resolveFieldCurrency`) and a format by type; `DetailView.tsx:1259` `percentField.scale ?? 0`; `PercentField.tsx` `declaredScale = percentField?.scale`; `ObjectForm.tsx:874-877` copies `min`/`max` only. No `apps/**` hit, no export face reads it, no `.js/.mjs` hit. So NO face reads the field-level `precision` as decimal places: the stop condition did not trigger.
- **objectstack's own readers: none.** `\.precision\b` over non-test `packages/**/*.ts` at head: `cli/src/commands/generate.ts:1687,2789` and `driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:18651` read `numeric.precision` where `numeric = numericColumnFor(type)` (the fixed `NUMERIC_COLUMN_REPRESENTATION`, `currency: EXACT`), never the field; `-w precision` over `packages/*/src` outside spec: comments only (objectql, formula, runtime, service-analytics read nothing). Inside spec: `CurrencyConfigSchema` (a different key), the #8321 conversion `field-malformed-scale-precision-removed` (shape only), `object.form.ts:189` offers the control with helpText `Total digits`. Storage, drivers, objectql, formula, analytics: no reader. Right.
- **No residual rule — judged right on the four axes.** Business need: nothing reads the key and no producer authors it (examples: 0 currency fields with a top-level `precision`; the only writer is the Studio control), so a residual (`precision` below the minor unit) would guard the internal consistency of an inert value. Long-term fit: a total-digit coherence rule belongs beside a total-digit ENFORCEMENT (DDL or the write seam) and neither exists; measured on main's `field.zod.ts`: `{ type: 'number', precision: 1, scale: 2 }` and `{ type: 'percent', precision: 0, scale: 3 }` both parse (byte-identical at head), so a currency-only, fixed-only remnant would be the one such rule in the spec. AI-authoring safety: the plausible AI mistake (`precision: 2` meaning decimals) is harmless because nothing renders from it, and the dispatch requires `precision: 2` to keep parsing; the real trap is the inert key, which is a finding (③), not a rule. Startup focus: no new gate. The site comment forbids reinstating a comparison, which is the right guard against an "improvement".
- **Test block: acceptance pins bear weight; no genuine refusal pin deleted.** Old block: 7 `it`s; new: 10. The two flipped pins are the widening itself: `rejects … (JPY + 2)` at `['precision']` → accepted with the authored value carried; `both anchors fire independently` → still `success: false`, now asserting exactly ONE issue at `['currencyConfig','precision']` with code, path, message and the `Declare \`precision: 0\`` prescription — the genuine refusal is still pinned through the `FieldSchema` door (and separately in the untouched `#7918 currencyConfig-level` block). Agreeing values (JPY 0, KWD 3) are subsumed by the digit-class loop; no-config, dynamic and non-currency pins kept; added: USD 18 carried, `ObjectSchema.create` round-trip, no-coherence parity. Ablation re-run here: head's test file against `origin/main:field.zod.ts` (anchor count 2 = the re-inserted field-level call + the `currencyConfig` one) → `6 failed | 24 passed (30)`, the six being exactly the new acceptance pins (USD 18, flipped JPY 2, digit-class loop, no-coherence parity, object door, both-keys-one-issue); restored file blob `26f8ef39` == head, then `30 passed (30)`. The pins bear weight. The `#11423` block and the digit-table block have no hunks.
- **Docs, sentence by sentence.** `field-types.mdx`: (a) "a `currency` field takes no `scale`: publish-time validation refuses the key" — TRUE on main: `field.zod.ts` `if (field.type === 'currency' && field.scale !== undefined) → path ['scale']` (#19629), pinned in `field-currency-scale-refused.test.ts`; the deleted `scale | Decimal places` row was therefore false on main, and deleting it is right. (b) "The field-level `precision` is the amount's total digit count — a DECIMAL(18,2) amount declares `precision: 18` — and is never compared with the currency" — TRUE as the key's declared meaning (describe `Total digits (non-negative integer)`, form helpText `Total digits`, generated `references/data/field.mdx:70`) and true at head for the comparison; it states a MEANING, not an enforcement — storage is the fixed `numericColumnFor('currency')` column and no face reads the key — so the DECIMAL(18,2) example teaches a sizing the platform does not perform. Not false; flagged in ③. (c) The `currencyConfig.precision` paragraph is the old rule re-keyed: TRUE for the rule at head; "Omit `currencyConfig.precision` to let renderers derive the width from the currency itself" implies a reader for that key, and objectui at the pin reads `currencyConfig.precision` nowhere (one comment hit, `CurrencyField.tsx:74`) — pre-existing wording, #19992's region, flagged in ③. `validation-rules.mdx:155`: TRUE (the field-level key is not compared). The unchanged "Precision defaults to 2 decimal places" sentence is the `currencyConfig` default, pre-existing.
- **Changeset body claims.** "Nothing that parsed before is refused now" and "output of every previously accepted field is byte-identical": TRUE (issue-only removal). "`scale` on a `currency` field is still refused": TRUE (above).

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset and `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body. Both spellings are the legal pair in `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (`yes` / `yes (widening)` — "both take at least `minor`"). `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis (clause ② declared ⇒ at least one moved package graded `minor` or above) is satisfied by `spec: minor`; a `fix(` type may raise a bump but never lower it, so `minor` stands. The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head is `success`. Level and wording are right for a widening that removes a ruling-installed refusal: the accept set grows, nothing is renamed or retired, no consumer migrates.
- **ADR-0087 entry rightly absent.** `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` `breakingDeclaration()` fires on `major`, `**BREAKING`, a `!` summary, or a `Clause-②` arm reading `narrowing` — its own docblock: "A widening is not a break". Precedent: `.changeset/19320-percent-storage-scale-derivation.md` (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `spec`+`objectql` minor, 36 cells refused→accepted, no ADR-0087 marker) — the precedent ruling 乙 item 4 itself names. The #7918 field-level refusal never had a ledger entry (`7918` occurs nowhere under `packages/spec/src/migrations`), so there is no entry to retire or amend; the `#7918` changeset is not in stock (released in v17). The removed refusal is recorded where a widening is recorded: the changeset body and the site comment.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The field-level `precision` key has no reader anywhere, and the liveness ledger's `live` verdict rests on retired evidence.** `packages/spec/liveness/field.json` `props.precision` reads `live` (verifiedAt 2026-08-10) citing objectui `@11c1e71e` reads at `CurrencyField.tsx:45`, `PercentField.tsx:13`, `index.tsx:662`, `useColumnSummary.ts:261`; at the pin `f8a9d0fb` all four are gone (CurrencyField derives from the currency; PercentField, the percent cell and the footer read `scale`). The `Spec property liveness` check-run is green on this head, so that gate does not re-measure cross-repo evidence at the pin. Meanwhile `object.form.ts:189` and objectui's `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:917-919` offer and write the key on every numeric type: an author writing `precision: 10` expecting a DECIMAL(10, s) bound gets nothing (DDL is fixed, the write seam reads `scale` only). ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove applies. The seat reports it folded into #19992 (same family, `currencyConfig.precision` no-reader); #19992 is outside this review's inputs, so the fold is reported, not verified here. Not this PR's to fix; this PR does not make it worse (the check it removes enforced nothing about total digits either).
- **Published text claiming the old field-level rule: none found at head.** `fraction digits` / `contradicts it` / `must agree` over the whole tree (excluding CHANGELOGs): only the two rewritten docs pages, the `scale` describe rows (which state the currency-minor-unit contract), `releases/v17/index.mdx:175` (history) and `field.test.ts:891` (a reference to the `.overwrite` shape). Generated `references/data/field.mdx:70` `precision | Total digits` and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:175` (`currencyConfig.precision: 2` on fixed USD, agreeing) are consistent. The remaining `#7918 currency precision twin` comment at `field.zod.ts:2458` refers to #11423 (the `currencyConfig` anchor) and stays accurate. `currency-fraction-digits.ts` docblock now says ⛔ not for the field-level key.
- **Docs sentence with an implied reader.** "Omit `currencyConfig.precision` to let renderers derive the width from the currency itself" (`field-types.mdx:175-176`) — renderers derive the width from the currency whether or not the key is declared; the sentence is the #7918 message's own wording re-keyed and belongs to #19992's resolution.
- **Authority chain.** The anchor was installed under the 2026-08-12 #7918 ruling (Option A); its removal rests on ruling 乙 (5805782503, item 3 names reading the field-level `precision` as decimal places as wrong) plus triage's re-derivation (5820411734, which carries its own 「如果维护者另有看法，以维护者为准」). The maintainer has not been asked in one word to confirm retiring the FIELD-level anchor specifically. The derivation is sound (the key's declared meaning and 乙 leave the #7918 rule with exactly one key whose meaning is decimal places, `currencyConfig.precision`, which keeps it), and this record is the at-tier review the claim named; recorded so the maintainer sees the step.
- **In-place docs deviation.** The dev deleted the `scale` row without a board scan (condition 3 unverified by dev); the seat reports #20170 as the only other open PR on these pages (frontmatter only, clean `merge-tree`). Outside this review's inputs; noted as reported.
- **Check-runs at this head** (final poll): 39 total — 34 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 in progress, 0 failing (Test Core 1-6, Dogfood 1-3, Type Check lanes, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Console Pin Gate skipped, all complete).

**VERDICT: PASS**
